gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the A1 mini's two headline numbers, 500 mm/s top speed and 'sub 48 dB' noise, on the same basis. Owners describe the quiet figure as a silent-mode result: silent mode runs at about 50% speed, and the part-cooling fan at 100% is said to go above 48 dB. Bambu's own spec page could not be opened to confirm the condition.
standout_why: I opened 3dprintgearlab.com (rank 1). It gives build volume and prices only, with no speed, acceleration or noise figures. Its only tolerance numbers are slicer settings: 0.2 mm clearance and -0.15 to -0.2 mm first-layer horizontal expansion. I opened extruly.com (cited). It gives 180 × 180 mm, 150 mm/s outer walls and a 60–70 mm minimum model size on the stock 0.4 mm nozzle, and it mentions '≤48 dB' only through an accessory listing, with no condition. Tom's Hardware (cited) and TechRadar came back truncated, so I could not check them. The rivals do not say under what condition the noise figure holds. But my own evidence for that condition is from forum users and is not on a Bambu page I could open, so it only partly stands out.
decides: It confirms the A1 mini rather than changing the pick. For fidget toys the slower, quieter mode costs little. extruly already advises dropping outer walls to 150 mm/s for clean print-in-place joints, which is well below the 500 mm/s headline. So the speed spec should not decide between the A1 mini and the A1. Build size (180 vs 256 mm) and the AMS lite colour option decide it. The page can say plainly that the quiet figure and the fast figure are not reached at the same time.
candidates: Bambu Lab A1 mini Combo (AMS lite)
